title: 08. Browser state and two-tab interface
description:

Implement a dependency-free accessible browser client using the shared API/event contracts:
- Require nonblank user-entered Client name and a .txt export before Generate. One export represents one client. Show shared progress then independent department statuses; prefill recipients from public configured department addresses.
- Provide Operations and Administration tabs with accessible keyboard behavior and separate recipient, subject, body, Save, Copy, Retry, and Regenerate controls as applicable.
- Keep each departments candidate, saved identity, edits, error, and saving status independent. Failure in one tab cannot erase or disable usable content in the other; retry only the failed department.
- Parse NDJSON according to shared contracts: analysis once; one outcome per requested department before done; terminal shared error instead on shared failure; reject truncated streams and duplicate outcomes. Keep valid independent successful results.
- Copy subject and body for manual sending; keep recipient separately visible/editable. Save each draft independently, retaining editable/copyable content on save failure.
- Group saved history by entered client name, clearly label department, and reopen saved drafts without transcript or analysis. No separate client-management feature.
- Keep file and temporary analysis in memory only. Refresh requires re-upload for regeneration; no localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, service workers, or Cache API for user content.
- Regenerate only the selected department into a new unsaved candidate, optionally linked to its saved parent. Protect unsaved edits from accidental replacement; preserve saved versions.
- Clear stale analysis when a new export is selected; process updated exports as fresh entire-history analysis and prevent stale responses from replacing newer client state.
- Confirm deletion, provide visible focus and accessible error/progress announcements, and keep controls usable at 375px width with 44px targets. No sending/assignment/language/owner/deadline controls.

Shared constraints: Follow the approved 2026-09-18 plan revision and shared contracts in src/contracts.ts; reuse src/config.ts limits and src/errors.ts stable errors. Single-user, one export per client, required user-entered client name (never inferred from sender nicknames), English-only outputs. Every new export processes the entire history. Keep transcripts, source references, and analysis in memory; D1 stores only explicitly saved drafts. No monitoring, sending, Send button, mailto, language selector, action owners, assignment selectors/categories, action deadlines, invented follow-ups, or representative-export quality-review feature/release gate. Preserve relevant client/project timing. Use runtime validation at API/model boundaries and do not silently truncate substantive conversations.

title: 07. API routing and streaming
description:
Source: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-16-whatsapp-chat-email-drafter.md — Implementation Tasks §7: API routing and streaming (lines 208–216).

Relevant files: src/index.ts; src/contracts.ts; src/config.ts; src/errors.ts; src/validation.ts; src/transcript.ts; src/analysis.ts; src/generation.ts; src/drafts.ts; test/*.test.ts.

Implement the source plan API table, multipart decoding, strict JSON validation, method errors, and draft CRUD:
- GET /api/config: public department names/addresses and upload limit, excluding credentials.
- POST /api/generate: multipart transcript and required clientName; initial validation/parsing occurs before streaming; stream shared analysis then independent department attempts.
- POST /api/generate/department: client name, department, validated temporary analysis, optional parent draft ID; stream only selected department. Revalidate analysis schema/references/size as untrusted data, never instructions or authenticity proof.
- GET /api/drafts: saved drafts newest updated first. GET /api/drafts/:id: one saved draft. POST /api/drafts: validated DraftCandidate, HTTP 201. PUT /api/drafts/:id: recipient/subject/body only. DELETE /api/drafts/:id: HTTP 204.
- Bound request bodies before fully buffering, including uploads, temporary analysis, and draft bodies; enforce configured serialized-size limits.
- Implement backpressure-aware NDJSON: stage for real shared/department progress; analysis once after shared analysis succeeds; department_result with department and unsaved candidate; department_error with department, stable code/message/retryable; error for terminal shared/pipeline failure; done for completed requested attempts including partial success.
- Each requested department gets exactly one result or error before done; shared failure terminates with one error instead. No events follow terminal events. Limits discovered during analysis yield stream errors. Isolate department errors so successful work survives.
- Stop active and queued work on cancellation; handle writer disconnection without unhandled rejections.
- Log route, duration, HTTP status, safe size metrics, and application error codes, including streamed department errors despite HTTP 200. Never log client names, transcripts, prompts, analysis, or email bodies; never expose raw provider/SQL errors. Generation must not write to D1.

Shared constraints: Follow the approved 2026-09-18 plan revision and shared contracts in src/contracts.ts; reuse src/config.ts limits and src/errors.ts stable errors. Single-user, one export per client, required user-entered client name (never inferred from sender nicknames), English-only outputs. Every new export processes the entire history. Keep transcripts, source references, and analysis in memory; D1 stores only explicitly saved drafts. No monitoring, sending, Send button, mailto, language selector, action owners, assignment selectors/categories, action deadlines, invented follow-ups, or representative-export quality-review feature/release gate. Preserve relevant client/project timing. Use runtime validation at API/model boundaries and do not silently truncate substantive conversations.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid requests before model invocation, partial-success stream contract, terminal event handling, disconnection, safe error responses, and no generation writes to D1.
notes: Implemented src/index.ts API factory, bounded strict request validation, prestream parsing and chunking, method routing and real D1 CRUD, normalized safe logs, backpressured NDJSON with exact outcomes and terminal events. Exported existing department request validator from src/generation.ts. Cancellation directly errors transform to unblock pending writes; catches writer closure and late model rejections. Added 53 API tests in test/api.test.ts using Workers local D1 and injected LLM. Final checks: 349 tests across 10 files; full typecheck; build; Worker deploy dry-run; 70 existing mocked desktop/mobile browser tests all pass. Frontend unchanged. No commit or deployment.

title: 04. Extract and reconcile the entire history
description:
Source: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-16-whatsapp-chat-email-drafter.md — Implementation Tasks §4: Extract and reconcile the entire history (lines 171–183).

Relevant files: src/analysis.ts; src/transcript.ts; src/llm.ts; src/validation.ts; src/contracts.ts; src/config.ts; src/errors.ts; test/*.test.ts; test/fixtures/*.txt.

Implement shared full-history analysis once per initial upload:
- Extract ordered conversation segments, substantive outcomes, explicit requests/commitments, completion evidence, and client overview facts with temporary source references. Use stable conversation IDs and source message references. Include unresolved substantive conversations; omit greetings and purely social exchanges.
- Detect topic changes inside time-bounded sessions; later returns to a topic remain new chronological conversations.
- Reconcile adjacent chunk edges so computational boundaries neither create paragraphs nor conceal topic changes; enforce mandatory gaps of at least six hours. Midnight alone is not a boundary.
- Keep outcome summaries local to each conversation, without rewriting earlier outcomes with future knowledge.
- Reconcile actions over the entire history: later clear textual completion removes earlier requests; deduplicate repeated references to the same request. Completed action events may exist internally for reconciliation.
- Keep ambiguous completion pending with Completion not confirmed. Attachment placeholders and vague acknowledgments alone do not establish completion. Pending actions contain description, supporting references, and uncertainty flag, with no owner/assignment/deadline fields or invented follow-ups.
- Preserve relevant timing in summaries/client facts; resolve superseded overview facts to their latest stated values, without inventing unavailable facts.
- Generate English analysis usable by both departments. Delimit chat/model content as untrusted data in every model stage.
- Preserve source order despite concurrent extraction and report real progress. Shared-analysis failure prevents department synthesis. Enforce configured extraction/analysis/synthesis-input limits without silently dropping conversations. Never persist analysis or references.

Shared constraints: Follow the approved 2026-09-18 plan revision and shared contracts in src/contracts.ts; reuse src/config.ts limits and src/errors.ts stable errors. Single-user, one export per client, required user-entered client name (never inferred from sender nicknames), English-only outputs. Every new export processes the entire history. Keep transcripts, source references, and analysis in memory; D1 stores only explicitly saved drafts. No monitoring, sending, Send button, mailto, language selector, action owners, assignment selectors/categories, action deadlines, invented follow-ups, or representative-export quality-review feature/release gate. Preserve relevant client/project timing. Use runtime validation at API/model boundaries and do not silently truncate substantive conversations.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic fake-model integration cases cover cross-chunk conversations, topic returns, six-hour gaps, later completion, ambiguous attachments, unresolved questions, empty actions, and absence of speculative tasks. These tests verify processing contracts, not a claim that schema validation guarantees semantic accuracy.
close_reason: Implemented src/analysis.ts and test/analysis.test.ts: bounded concurrent extraction, full-history evidence reconciliation, chronological boundary/coverage guards, explicit action evidence, memory-only stable references, cancellation and progress. Focused analysis/parser/LLM/validation: 169 tests passed; typecheck passed.

title: 05. Generate independent department drafts
description:
Source: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-16-whatsapp-chat-email-drafter.md — Implementation Tasks §5: Generate independent department drafts (lines 185–195).

Relevant files: src/generation.ts; src/analysis.ts; src/llm.ts; src/validation.ts; src/contracts.ts; src/config.ts; src/errors.ts; test/*.test.ts.

Implement independently validated department synthesis from shared analysis:
- Operations: one outcome-focused paragraph of 1–3 concise sentences per substantive conversation, in chronology, followed by one consolidated pending-action list. Include unresolved substantive conversations; omit social-only exchanges; no total-length cap may silently drop conversations. Outcomes remain local to each conversation. Pending actions use latest full-export state and explicit requests/commitments only; ambiguous completion is Completion not confirmed. If none remain, use exactly: No pending actions identified in the chat.
- Administration: concise overview of supported stated client/company identity, service needs, scope, location, latest stated budget, timing, requirements, enquiry status, and agreed commercial terms. Omit unavailable details.
- Require English subject/body for both. Validate model output before application code maps configured department recipients; never accept model-supplied recipients. Recipients are defaults editable by the user.
- Isolate synthesis outcomes and error boundaries so either department can succeed independently; preserve successful editable/saveable work when the other fails.
- Return validated temporary analysis to browser memory for department-only retry/regeneration. Revalidate schema, source references, and size on every request; treat it as untrusted data, never instructions/authenticity proof, with no configured recipients in analysis.
- Retry only the failed department. Regenerate only the chosen department into a fresh unsaved DraftCandidate, optionally linked by parent_draft_id to its saved parent.

title: 02. Parse exports and establish time boundaries
description:
Source: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-16-whatsapp-chat-email-drafter.md — Implementation Tasks §2: Parse exports and establish time boundaries (lines 147–158).

Relevant files: src/transcript.ts; src/contracts.ts; src/config.ts; src/errors.ts; test/*.test.ts; test/fixtures/*.txt.

Implement export parsing and chronological message chunking:
- Support iOS bracketed and Android dashed records, Arabic/Latin digits, optional seconds, 12/24-hour times, multiline messages, and bidi/BOM cleanup.
- Validate real date/time headers with fixed day/month/year interpretation. Arbitrary bracketed continuation lines must not become message headers.
- Preserve source order and stable message references. Calculate time gaps from local export timestamps without assuming a timezone.
- Reject invalid or backward timestamps with clear parsing errors rather than guessing chronology.
- Filter only recognized whole system-notice/attachment-placeholder records; preserve ordinary messages mentioning those phrases and substantive captions.
- Treat missing attachments as unavailable evidence, never proof of completion.
- Mark mandatory conversation boundaries at gaps of at least six hours. Crossing midnight alone is not a boundary.
- Chunk complete messages within configured message/chunk/count/serialized-size limits. Computational chunks do not define conversation paragraphs. Topic boundaries and chunk-edge reconciliation belong to analysis; retain enough boundary/reference information for that work.

Shared constraints: Follow the approved 2026-09-18 plan revision and shared contracts in src/contracts.ts; reuse src/config.ts limits and src/errors.ts stable errors. notes: Implemented src/transcript.ts; exclusive tests test/transcript.test.ts and test/fixtures/transcript-{ios,android-arabic,filtering}.txt. No shared source/config/package changes required. Interface: parseTranscript(text: string, limits: TranscriptLimits = DEFAULT_LIMITS): TranscriptMessage[]; chunkTranscript(messages: readonly TranscriptMessage[], limits: TranscriptLimits = DEFAULT_LIMITS): TranscriptChunk[]. TranscriptLimits is exported Pick<Limits, maxUploadBytes|maxTranscriptChars|maxMessageChars|maxChunkChars|maxChunks>; pass config.limits. API must bound actual file/request bytes before decoding, then run BOTH functions before model invocation/streaming. Parser additionally bounds decoded UTF-8 bytes/raw chars and full multiline message text. IDs message-N and zero-based indices count all source records, including removed recognized notices (gaps intentional); timestamps YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss are local, no Z/timezone; two-digit years map to 2000–2099. Source order preserved, equal timestamps accepted, invalid/backward timestamps rejected including filtered records. boundary_before is true on first retained record and retained-record gaps >=6 hours, independent of chunk edges. Whole known system notices removed only without sender; unknown notices/substantive captions preserved. Recognized whole attachment placeholders normalized to kind=attachment and text=Attachment unavailable; contents and completion cannot be verified. Analysis must never treat these as completion proof. Chunk IDs chunk-N, indices zero-based; full JSON.stringify(chunk).length includes references, escaping and envelope; messages not split and boundary flags not changed. Errors use shared AppError: PARSE_ERROR, UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE, TRANSCRIPT_TOO_LARGE, MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE, CHUNK_TOO_LARGE, TOO_MANY_CHUNKS.
